title: Hˢ machine-epsilon conformance — one test, every collective member
purpose: A single, fixed-vector test that every collective member runs in their own environment to confirm Hˢ's D=4 exactness sits at the IEEE-754 double-precision floor. Fixed inputs (no RNG) mean every conformant float64 platform must return the SAME numbers and the SAME receipt — that identity IS the conformance.
human_gate: Peter Higgins is the sole gate. He has already run and confirmed the reference result. Each AI member runs the identical test and reports its own numbers; nothing here is submitted or pushed.
honest_broker: Tier 1 (measured). The receipt is over full-precision reprs because the residuals live below the 12-decimal canonicalization round (they would otherwise hash to 0.0). A member 'passes' only by reproducing the reference values bit-for-bit at the floor; a deviation is a real finding, not a rounding nuisance.

the_test.claim_under_test: A four-part composition's three ILR coordinates are the imaginary part of a quaternion, and an Aitchison rotation acts as the exact sandwich q·v·q* = R(q)·v on S³≅SU(2), reproduced to the IEEE floor; norm is preserved exactly.

fixed_inputs.note: q = qraw / ||qraw||. Helmert-ILR basis (the engine's). All float64. No random numbers — identical across languages.

steps: 1. Report the platform float64 machine epsilon; it MUST equal 2.220446049250313e-16 (IEEE-754 double).
2. v = Helmert_ILR(clr(x)) — the composition's ILR coordinates.
3. Test A: residA = max|q·(0,v)·q* (imag part) − R(q)·v|, where R(q) is the SO(3) matrix from q.
4. Test B (ILR-independent): v2=[0.5,-0.5,0.25]; residB = max|q·(0,v2)·q* − R(q)·v2|.
the_test.pass_rule: VERDICT = PASS iff machine_eps == 2.220446049250313e-16 AND worst_case <= 16·eps (= 3.552713678800501e-15). Report the actual numbers regardless.

expected_reference_values.worst_case: 1.1102230246251565e-16  (= eps/2, i.e. one ULP at this magnitude)

the_test.receipt_canonicalization: sha256 over json.dumps({machine_eps,norm_preservation,residA_sandwich_vs_SO3,residB_plain_vector,test,verdict,worst_case} as FULL-PRECISION STRING reprs, sort_keys=True, separators=(', ', ': '), UTF-8).
the_test.core_receipt_fields: {machine_eps, residA_sandwich_vs_SO3, residB_plain_vector, test, verdict} — the implementation-INVARIANT exactness fields. This is the receipt that every conformant float64 platform must match; it carries the actual D=4 exactness claim.
the_test.full_receipt_note: parity_receipt_sha256 (1f545c2d...) ALSO includes norm_preservation + worst_case, which run through sqrt+reduction and vary by 0–1 ULP across BLAS/numpy versions. A full-receipt MISMATCH with a core-receipt MATCH is the expected, honest signature of norm-evaluation order — not a failure of the algebra.

language_agnostic_pseudocode: qmul(a,b): Hamilton product of two quaternions [w,x,y,z].
R(q) for unit q=[w,x,y,z]: the standard 3x3 rotation matrix.
helmert(4): rows i=1..3, B[i-1,0:i]=1/i, B[i-1,i]=-1, scale by sqrt(i/(i+1)).
sandwich(q,v) = imag part of qmul(qmul(q,[0,v]), qconj(q)).
residA = max_abs(sandwich(q,v) - R(q)@v); compare to machine eps.

how_to_update: When a member returns its run, fill that member's row (machine_eps, residA, residB, norm_preservation, worst_case, verdict, receipt_match, confirmed_by, date) and set verdict PASS/FAIL by the pass_rule. A FAIL or a receipt mismatch is a real cross-platform finding to investigate (e.g., fused-multiply-add reordering, non-IEEE float), not something to paper over.
what_a_clean_sweep_proves: 5/5 reported. This is the citable cross-platform claim for P1 (Tier-1) and satisfies the P-2 cross-platform gate for P3. findings.title: norm_preservation is 1-ULP platform-variant; the sandwich residuals are not
findings.observed: reference + Grok: norm_preservation=0.0 (full receipt 1f545c2d matches). ChatGPT (Python 3.13.5/numpy 2.3.5): norm_preservation=eps=2.220446049250313e-16, worst_case=eps; full receipt 48745b81 differs, but machine_eps/residA/residB/verdict identical => CORE receipt 06ccdb25 matches.
findings.cause: norm_preservation = | ||sand|| - ||v|| | evaluates a square-root over a summed reduction; numpy/BLAS reduction order differs between versions, giving 0 or 1 ULP. The sandwich-vs-SO(3) residuals are direct multiply-adds in fixed order and reproduce bit-for-bit everywhere.
findings.consequence: The bit-for-bit portable invariant is the CORE receipt (the exactness claim). norm preservation holds to <=1 ULP but its exact bit value is NOT a portable parity field. This protects P1/P3 from overclaiming an all-member identical full receipt while preserving the real result: D=4 exactness is platform-independent at the IEEE floor.
findings.credit: ChatGPT (claim audit) — flagged the mismatch instead of papering over it; verified independently in-session.

paper_wording: HS-EPS-1 reproduces the quaternion sandwich-vs-SO(3) residuals at 1.1102230246251565e-16 (one ULP) bit-for-bit across independent implementations (the core conformance receipt), establishing platform-independent D=4 exactness at the IEEE-754 double-precision floor. Norm preservation holds to within one machine epsilon; its exact bit value is implementation-dependent (norm-reduction order) and is therefore reported but excluded from the bit-for-bit receipt.
